brief: Following a prior call for tactical European outperformance, last week's unwind in the AI trade (the Nvidia scandal), weak post-IPO momentum for Anthropic, and renewed hawkish Fed concern hit US equities hardest: S&P 500 -8.61%, Nasdaq 100 -10.43% (sharpest weekly declines since the pandemic and April 2025), Nikkei -7.70%, STOXX 600 -5.17%, SMI -3.53%, EEM -11.62%. The declines broke key technical levels, invalidating Pictet's prior extended wave (3) scenario (161.8% projection 7,744, target 8,218-8,747) and confirming a wave (4) correction: S&P 500 support at 6,817 then 6,182, needing a close above the 200-day SMA to signal stabilisation. Nasdaq 100 (next support 23,369), the Magnificent Seven/BM7P (below 32,600-32,800) and the SOX (below its 200-day SMA for the first time since March 2025) show similar or more advanced breakdowns. Breadth has not confirmed capitulation: only 5.57% of names are at new 52-week lows and 10.16% have RSI below 30, both below 2022/April-2025 extremes, so a tactical bounce is possible but a durable low is not yet confirmed. The 10-year yield holding above 4.80% suggests bonds still read this as consolidation, not a macro breakdown; a break below 4.80% toward 4.62% would both signal a trend change and add structural support for gold.
